facts.anchor: I saw the fires from my window again last night.
facts.fact: 叙述者昨夜又从窗口看见四野点燃的火堆，说这仪式每年如期而至。

facts.anchor: When he walked in and shook the water from his overcoat
facts.fact: Alexander S— 在雨里走进咖啡馆，抖落灰大衣上的水。

facts.anchor: Mrs Hayworth wasted no time flagging down a waiter to have him invited over
facts.fact: Mrs Hayworth 立刻招来侍者，把 Alexander 请到她们的桌边。

facts.anchor: ‘Charmed,’ he said, with another quick glance at me.
facts.fact: Mrs Hayworth 把叙述者介绍为「Maria Isabel」，Alexander 只说了句 Charmed 便坐下。

facts.anchor: Mr S— had found our meeting so pleasurable that he wished to repeat it.
facts.fact: 次日清晨，一封无字奶油色信封送到她房间，Alexander 在信中邀她下午去海滨长廊散步。

facts.anchor: I scribbled a response, beneath his own words
facts.fact: 她在他字句下方草草写了回信交信差带回，且没有告诉 Mrs Hayworth。

facts.anchor: ‘How do you find Scotland, Ms Smith?’
facts.fact: Alexander 开车带她到海边，挽着她散步时问她觉得苏格兰如何。

facts.anchor: his voice asking me if I would like to drive around a bit
facts.fact: 骤雨把两人赶回车里，他又问她要不要再开车兜一圈，好把相处时间拖长。

relations: 叙述者本名 Maria Isabel，Mrs Hayworth 坚持用全名「Maria Isabel」称她，她本人要求只叫 Isabel；Alexander 在本章称她「Ms Smith」。Mrs Hayworth 是带她游历英国寻父的旅伴兼引路人（自称出力最多），与 Alexander 只是「acquaintances of sorts」的泛泛之交，且视他为有身份的可婚男子（an eligible bachelor of a certain pedigree）。叙述者称他「Mr S—」，他称她「Ms Smith」；Mrs Hayworth 称他「Mr S—」。
